questions.question: You stop completely at an intersection, let cross traffic and pedestrians pass, then continue when it is safe. This matches:
questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When you must stop at an intersection but see no stop line or crosswalk, you should:

options.text: Slow down to check if cross traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see at least 200 feet in both directions, even if you enter the intersecting roadway.
Stop where you can see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.
questions.explanation: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the nearest point where you can see approaching traffic. Do not enter the intersecting roadway just to get a better view.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass only from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that workers may be on or near the road ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Enter faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of highway traffic. Signal, find an opening, speed up to match traffic, then merge safely.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, weather, road conditions, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow center line. You immediately know that:

options.text: Traffic flows in one direction only.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows in both directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means you can pass slower traffic when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If an oncoming vehicle has high beams on, look toward the ____ side of the road.
questions.correctAnswerText: Right
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road when an oncoming vehicle has high beams on. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: Your rearview mirror should let you see:

options.text: Most of the lane beside you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The entire rear window.
questions.explanation: Adjust your rearview mirror so you can see the entire rear window from the driver's seat. You should move only your eyes to use this mirror, not your head.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks have the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow background. They alert you to upcoming hazards. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Adjust your speed as needed to drive safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic only goes in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic only goes in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A one-way sign means traffic only flows in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill, turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system in your vehicle is dangerous because it can cause:
questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful fumes from your vehicle. A leak lets these fumes into the passenger area. This can cause carbon monoxide poisoning. Fix any leaks right away.

questions.question: ____ of crashes happen within 25 miles of home.
questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: 75 percent of crashes happen within 25 miles of home. Always wear your seat belt before you leave your driveway, even for short trips.

questions.question: When you are in a line of traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
Make sure your vehicle can cross the entire track without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross the entire track without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough space to cross completely without stopping. Never pass other vehicles at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: Red pavement markings or reflectors mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter this roadway.
questions.explanation: Red markings or reflectors mean you must not enter that roadway. If you see red reflectors or markings, turn around.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect how far it takes to stop your vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change with your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. You should:

options.text: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors and signal before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads:

options.text: Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.
Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, avoid sudden speed or direction changes. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: Which of these direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning on some highways?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows in lanes show which lanes to use for specific actions like driving straight or turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: A divided highway is ahead. The road splits into two one-way lanes separated by a divider. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow traffic light?

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
Slow down and stop if you can do so safely.
Turn left after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Turn freely because you have the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to your current lane.
The lane marked with an arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your current lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane closest to where you came from. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same as a red circular light.
You may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a red circular light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a regular red light. You must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are driving over a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that your road intersects with a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: When should you start speeding up during a turn?

options.text: At the halfway point of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the halfway point of the turn.
questions.explanation: Speed up once you reach the middle of the turn. Keep looking ahead along your path.

questions.question: If you double your speed, how much does the force of impact increase?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four times.
questions.explanation: Faster speeds create much greater impact force in a crash. Doubling your speed increases the force of impact by four times.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on a freeway shoulder?

options.text: If you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except during an emergency.

questions.question: What does the "P" stand for in the SIPDE driving method?
questions.correctAnswerText: Predict hazards.
questions.explanation: The "P" stands for "Predict hazards." Think about the worst thing that could happen while driving and plan how you would react to stay safe.
